pages.summary: The desktop's windows brought forward: the Command Window, the Command History, the Workspace and the Current Folder.
body: Each shows its window (as a tab of its group when the windows are docked) and `commandwindow` also gives it the keyboard, so a program can hand back to the person at the Command Window when it has finished.
syntax: The Command Window, with the keyboard.

examples.title: A program that ends by showing its results

pages.summary: A variable opened in the Variables view, to look at and edit as a table.
body: The name is a variable's, or a part of one such as `'s.data'` or `'c{2}'`.
PyLAB answers with its own name: `Release` is `"PyLAB"`, `Stage` `"release"`, `Update` 0 and the date not known.
In the page Python runs in one thread; the number can be set (and the old one is given back), so programs that set it run unchanged.
syntax: Set, the old number given back.

pages.summary: The memory the engine uses and can have.
body: In the page this is the WebAssembly memory of its Python, which grows as needed up to 4 GB. With outputs, `userview` has the memory used by this engine and the largest array it can make, `systemview` the memory of the browser's process.

examples.title: The fields of the answer
examples.intro: The numbers depend on the computer and on what has been done, so only the fields are shown.

pages.summary: Whether the engine has a toolbox's functions.
body: `license('test', feature)` is true for the toolboxes PyLAB has functions of; feature names are toolboxes' names such as `'Statistics_Toolbox'`, `'Optimization_Toolbox'` or `'Signal_Toolbox'`, in any case. `'checkout'` answers the same with a message, and `'inuse'` lists them.
